### About Alice

![Alice logo](https://seedtable.com/api/logo/topic_images/1bfb7f8318d646b0a9915a25180c7c92.png)

[Alice](https://seedtable.com/companies/alice-io)

[Tel Aviv](https://seedtable.com/best-startups-in-tel-aviv), [Israel](https://seedtable.com/best-startups-in-israel)[Security](https://seedtable.com/best-cybersecurity-startups)439 employeesFounded 2018240.0M USD total raised [Website](https://alice.io/)

Alice is an AI governance and security company, founded in 2018 as ActiveFence and renamed in 2026. Its original technology detected malicious content online for social platforms' trust and safety teams, and that work continues alongside a newer line securing generative AI. The WonderSuite platform covers the AI lifecycle: WonderBuild stress-tests models and agents before launch, WonderFence applies runtime guardrails in production, and WonderCheck red-teams deployed systems continuously. Alice Labs runs its frontier research on model evaluation. The company says it protects more than 3 billion users across over 120 languages, and is co-headquartered in New York and Tel Aviv.

### About This Round

[Alice](https://seedtable.com/companies/alice-io) raised $140 million in a Series D announced on 25 August 2026 and led by [Apax Digital](https://seedtable.com/companies/apax-digital) [1](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/a8lj22cfo). [Samsung](https://seedtable.com/companies/samsung), [SentinelOne](https://seedtable.com/companies/sentinelone), [Maj Invest](https://seedtable.com/companies/maj-invest), MoreTech, [Phoenix Insurance](https://seedtable.com/companies/phoenix-insurance-company), [Norwest](https://seedtable.com/companies/norwest-venture-partners), CRV, [Resolute Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/resolute-ventures), [Grove Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/grove-ventures), [Highland Europe](https://seedtable.com/companies/highland-europe), Vintage Investments, [NFX](https://seedtable.com/companies/nfx) and [Claltech](https://seedtable.com/investors/claltech) also took part. The round takes total raised to $280 million. Calcalist puts the valuation at $700-800 million; the company did not disclose a figure, and its chief executive has separately been quoted putting it closer to $1 billion.[1](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/a8lj22cfo)

Alice was founded in 2018 as ActiveFence, and until a rebrand earlier in 2026 that is the name it traded under. Its original business was trust and safety - finding abusive and harmful content at scale for platforms. It now sells adversarial testing and runtime guardrails for AI models, working with frontier labs including Anthropic, Google and Nvidia during training to simulate malicious prompts and harden models against jailbreaks and prompt-injection attacks, and selling enterprise guardrails on top.[2](https://www.securityweek.com/alice-raises-140m-to-expand-ai-model-defenses-and-enterprise-guardrails/)

The capital funds the expansion of that AI line. The company says its AI business has grown more than 500% over the past two years and that annual recurring revenue is approaching $100 million, with the chief executive Noam Schwartz remaining a co-founder and running the company from dual bases in Tel Aviv and New York.[3](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/25/alice-raises-140m-as-its-ai-security-business-grows-more-than-500/)

The arithmetic is the story here, and it cuts against the headline. A company approaching $100 million of ARR, valued at $800 million, is trading at roughly eight times revenue - unremarkable for enterprise software and conspicuously cheap for anything with 'AI security' in the description, a category where multiples of twenty and up have been routine. The most economical reading is that the market is pricing two businesses at once: a mature content-moderation book that grows like a services company, and an AI-safety book growing at 500% that is still small enough not to move the blended number. That also explains the syndicate. Samsung and SentinelOne are strategic buyers of exactly the second business, not the first; Apax Digital is a growth investor that underwrites cash flows. Whether the rebrand was worth doing is a question about which of those two lines is generating the ARR in eighteen months' time, and the company has not disclosed the split.
